html:
SMTO-CAP-0010 — SMTO tried to use a tool that isn't installed

GUID: 785a28e4-9266-4397-b0d9-4d5f0c602423
Slug: tool-not-registered
Domain: CAP · Subsystem: cap

What happened

  • SMTO's Agent asked for a tool by a name this SMTO doesn't have. Nothing was run, and SMTO won't swap in a similar-looking tool, because that could do something you didn't ask for.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Watch the Task for a moment. If it keeps working after this, you don't need to do anything. SMTO tells the Agent the name wasn't found, so it can pick a tool that really exists.
  2. If you expected a tool from a user Skill, open User Skills and check the Skill shows Ready to select. If it shows Disabled, select Enable. Tools from a disabled, removed or missing Skill aren't available to SMTO.
  3. Open Capabilities by the message box, select Refresh catalog, then ask SMTO to continue the Task. The Agent then works from the tools installed now instead of an old or guessed name.

What success looks like

  • The Task uses an installed tool and moves on without this message.

If it still fails

  • Send Copy error details to the person who manages SMTO; they show the tool name that was asked for. Don't ask SMTO to use an old tool name from before a Skill was updated; use the names in the refreshed list.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Capability registry lookup (CapabilityRegistry.get) or ToolCatalog.validate_name could not resolve the requested tool name to any installed capability (Tool not registered or unknown_tool_name); nothing executed.

What this means

  • Registry lookup or tool-name validation cannot resolve the requested identity to an installed capability. Capability discovery and registration describe what this run may request. They do not grant operating-system permission, override exclusions or authorize execution by themselves.

Why this can happen

  • Registry lookup or tool-name validation cannot resolve the requested identity to an installed capability.

How to diagnose it

  • Check the exact registered capability identity separately from whether it has been advertised or excluded in this run.

How to fix it

  • Check the requested ID against registry.tool_ids() and the run's catalog (src/agent_runtime/capabilities/registry.py; validate_name in src/agent_runtime/native/catalog.py). If the tool belongs to a removed, disabled or renamed Skill, restore or update that Skill on /skills; otherwise have the Agent rediscover with discover_tools and use an exact registered ID.
  • Refresh discovery and use an exact registered tool. Restore or update the required skill if its tool is missing.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • The intended identity resolves to the installed capability and its current declaration.

What not to do

  • Do not submit a stale identifier or revision after another actor changed the resource.

Technical notes

  • Capability discovery and registration describe what this run may request. They do not grant operating-system permission, override exclusions or authorize execution by themselves.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
